 PUBLIC COMMENT RULES
 “(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
 (a) Every agenda for regular meetings shall provide an opportunity for members of the
 public to directly address the legislative body on any item of interest to the public, before
 or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter
 jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action shall be taken on any item not
 appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise authorized by subdivision (b) of
 Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

City Council  Wednesday, June 26, 2024
  (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
 that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
 limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
 each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
 time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
 the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
 a local agency.”

 In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
 of two (2) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, Appointment(s), New
 Business and Closed Session, with two (2) minutes on each Public Hearing, and, if
 desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items not on the agenda that are within the
 subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker
 utilizing a translator will receive twice the amount of time specified.

   City Council Staff Report
DATE:  JUNE 26, 2024

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  OPERATIONS DEPARTMENT
  FINANCE DIVISION

DISTRICT:  ALL

SUBJECT:  APPROVE PROJECT AUTHORIZATION A UNDER MASTER
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH NBS GOVERNMENT FINANCE
  GROUP TO PROVIDE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT AND COMMUNITY
  FACILITY ADMINISTRATION, OTHER RELATED CONSULTING
  SERVICES, AND CONTINUING DISCLOSURE SERVICES IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $1,160,000 FOR A TERM OF FIVE (5)
  YEARS

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Project Authorization A under Master Services Agreement No. A-8883
  with NBS Government Finance Group to provide Assessment District and
  Community Facility District administration, other related consulting services, and
  continuing disclosure services in an amount not to exceed $1,160,000 for a term
  of five (5) years; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Project Authorization A
  under Master Services Agreement No. A-8883 with NBS Government Finance
  Group, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

NBS has assisted the City with managing and reporting on behalf of its Special
Financing Districts. The City’s Special Financing Districts include one Assessment
District and seven Community Facilities Districts that require continuous management
and reporting. Services include, but are not limited to, notice of special tax disclosures,
debt disclosures, delinquency monitoring, reminder and demand letters, data collection,
policy review, cost recovery, cash flow analysis, fund analysis, levy submittal, tax roll
removal and notice, foreclosure proceedings, resubmission of rejects, maintaining
parcel change data, annual reports, prepayment and recalculation of amortization
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Project Authorization A with NBS Government Finance Group
June 26, 2024
Page 2

schedules, bond calls, bond tenders, release of liens, notice of special assessment,
California Debt and Investment Advisory Commission reporting, and county assessor
reporting.

In addition to the administration services for Assessment District and Community
Facilities Districts, NBS provides the continuing disclosure services required by Federal
regulations for debts issued by the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency of the City
of Palmdale.

DISCUSSION

The existing agreement with NBS Government Finance Group will expire June 30, 2024.
To ensure the City remains compliant with District reporting, continuing disclosures,
delinquency management, and general administration, staff recommend that the City
Council approve Project Authorization A under the NBS Master Services Agreement.

FISCAL IMPACT

$1,160,000; the fiscal impact for the full term of five (5) years is $1,160,000. Funds for
Fiscal Year 2024-25 are proposed for appropriation through the annual operating budget.
Funding for future years will be proposed through the annual budget process for each
subsequent year.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  B. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.
  C. Involve and expand engagement to enhance public oversight and
  transparency.

This CONTRACT for services (“Contract” herein) is made and entered into by and
between the City of Palmdale, a public body corporate and politic, (hereinafter called

, (hereinafter called “CONTRACTOR”). This Contract shall become effective on the
date of the last signatory.

RECITALS

and is qualified to perform the services described in this Contract.

NOW THEREFORE, CITY and CONTRACTOR, in consideration of the mutual
covenants hereinafter set forth, agree as follows:

1  CITY PROJECT MANAGER

To provide the services required by this Contract, CONTRACTOR shall act under the
authority and approval of CITY Director/designee, who shall oversee this Contract,

information, audit billings, and approve payments. The CONTRACTOR shall channel

2  DESCRIPTION OF WORK

The following services, including but not limited to:
-Assessment District and Community Facilites District Administration
-Review of Policy
-Data Collection
-Fund Analysis
-Public Hearings
-Cost Recovery
-Scheduling
-Fiscal Goals
-Annual Reporting(s)
-Administrative Services
-Bond Formation Services
-Elections and Vote Tabulation
-CFD Bond Issuance
-Non-Bonded CFD Formation Services

1915 Act Assessment District Administration

KICK-OFF MEETING, PROJECT SCHEDULE

NBS will meet with City staff, legal counsel and other interested parties to:
•Establish lines of communication.
•Clarify the specific project goals and criteria that will meet the City’s preference.
•Identify and resolve any special circumstances that may be involved in the
administration of the districts.
•Develop project schedules to meet legal requirements and provide for effective
interaction of all involved parties.
•Establish meeting dates consistent with schedule to achieve project milestones.

DATA COLLECTION

NBS will gather and review data relevant to the administration of the Assessment
District. Data will be obtained from various sources, including City records,
Assessor’s parcel maps, and County Assessor information. NBS will maintain and
periodically update a database of all parcels within the district along with relevant
parcel information.

POLICY REVIEW

NBS will review policies and procedures that have been established by the City for
compliance with the governing documents and law. These policies will be
incorporated into our service to the City.

COST RECOVERY

  Concord - Document ID: 02wkkNhxKEkjiUkQRQDri4  1-16
 NBS will assist the City in identifying all costs associated with the administration of
the Assessment District and recover those costs through the levy process as outlined
in §8682 and §8682.1 of the California Streets and Highways Code. These costs may
include, but not be limited to Registrar/Transfer/Paying Agent fees, Arbitrage Rebate
calculation fees, bank fees, and expenses of the City and its consultants related to
the administration of the district.

FUND ANALYSIS

NBS will determine the balance requirements and acquire the current cash balances
for the district. We will make recommendations to ensure that the flow of funds and
fund balances are in compliance with bond documents. Cash flow analysis will also
be performed to determine any levy shortfall or surplus.

LEVY SUBMITTAL

NBS will submit the levy to the County Auditor-Controller in the required format.
Assessments rejected by the County Auditor-Controller will be researched and
resubmitted for collection on the County Tax Roll. Any parcels that are not accepted
by the County for collection will be invoiced with payment to be directed to the City.

MAINTAIN DISTRICT DATA

NBS will annually track all parcel changes to ensure that all changes are
documented. Historical parcel change and assessment apportionment data will be
maintained by NBS.

ANNUAL REPORT

NBS will provide a comprehensive Annual Report that will show a detailed listing of
the amounts submitted to the County or directly billed for collection, details of
delinquent assessments, fund analysis, paid off parcels, all bond call activity, and
assessed valuation information.

DELINQUENCY MONITORING

NBS will provide a comprehensive list of delinquencies after each installment
becomes due. The delinquency report will provide the district’s overall delinquency
percentage as well as a detailed list of each delinquent parcel, with the name and
address of the delinquent parcel owner, the delinquent amount, and penalties.

PREPAYMENT CALCULATION/AMORTIZATION SCHEDULE

NBS will provide assessment prepayment calculations and amortization schedules to
interested parties. The requester will pay the cost of this service; however, there will
be no charge to the City or property owners.

BOND CALLS

 NBS will prepare the spread of principal to be called within maturities for all bond calls
and coordinate the call with the Paying Agent/Trustee.

RELEASE OF LIENS

NBS will prepare all documents required to release the liens of parcels that have
prepaid the assessment.

NOTICE OF SPECIAL ASSESSMENT

disclosure notice.

Trust Indenture, Tax Certificate, and IRS form 8038-G to determine whether the issue
is subject to the rebate requirement and identify what general and/or elective
exceptions are available to the issue.

DATA COLLECTION

required for the reports.

BOND YIELD

Sources and uses of all proceeds will be identified to determine how the rebate
requirement applies to each fund. Produce a debt service schedule for the issue and
calculate and/or verify the bond yield.

EXCESS EARNINGS CALCULATION

Trust statements and/or City accounting records will be utilized to create a cash flow
report for each fund. These reports will be used to identify all investment activity and
interest earnings attributable to the funds. Calculate the arbitrage earnings on
investment of funds subject to rebate and determine the issuer’s net rebate and/or
penalty liability.

INVESTMENT YIELD CALCULATION

The investment yield will be calculated for each fund as a “reality check” to reaffirm
the accuracy of the cash flow report. This measure not only ensures the accuracy of
the report but also is a useful tool when analyzing investment opportunities.

SUMMARY REPORT

A report will be prepared that summarizes the rebate liability of the issue, identifies
the methodology employed, computational assumptions, conclusions, and any
recommended changes in record keeping and investment policies. Analyze all
transactions and explore every legally permissible avenue to minimize the rebate
liability. Identify outstanding proceeds subject to the rebate requirement, and identify
the instruments and yields of the investment vehicles utilized by each fund.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-053, a
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Palmdale establishing an appropriations limit
for Fiscal Year 2024-25 pursuant to Article XIII B of the Constitution of the State of
California and repeal Resolution No. CC 2023-042.

BACKGROUND

Article XII B of the California State Constitution, more commonly referred to as the Gann
Initiative or Gann Appropriations Limit (Limit), was adopted by California voters in 1980.
The Limit places restrictions on the amount of tax proceeds that state and local
governmental agencies can receive and appropriate each fiscal year.

The Limit is calculated based on the actual amount of tax proceeds appropriated during
the 1978-79 Fiscal Year and is increased each year for inflation and population growth.
Inflationary adjustments are, by law, based on the growth in the California Per Capita
Income or the growth in non-residential assessed valuation due to new construction
within the City. Population adjustments are based on the population growth of the City
or the population growth within the City’s county. The decision as to which of the options
to select is made annually by a recorded vote of the City Council.

The statutes regarding the adoption of the Limit, contained in Government Code Section
7910, require the governing body to annually adopt, by resolution, an appropriations
limit each year for the following fiscal year.

DISCUSSION

For Fiscal Year 2024-25, the City estimates that tax proceeds to be received, as well as
tax proceeds appropriated by the City Council, will continue to be under the legal limit.
The City’s appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2024-25 is established at $171,208,963,
a 3.60 percent increase over the Fiscal Year 2023-24 limit. This is the maximum amount
of tax proceeds the City will be able to receive and appropriate in the coming fiscal year.
The City’s appropriations, subject to the limit for Fiscal Year 2024-25, are estimated to
be $113,971,313. Therefore, the City’s Fiscal Year 2024-25 adopted budget
appropriations subject to the limit are $57,237,650 less than the appropriations limit.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement with Hinderliter, de Llamas & Associates for Sales, Use, and
  Transaction Tax Audit and Information Services in an amount not to exceed
  $262,000 for a five (5) year term; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute the Agreement No. A-
  8885 with Hinderliter, de Llamas & Associates, including minimal and/or non-
  substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

On an annual basis, the City uses Hinderliter, de Llamas & Associates (HdL) to provide
Sales, Use, and Transaction Tax databases for ongoing reports, analysis, and ad hoc
services. In addition, the firm provides sales tax audit and recovery work that redirects
misallocated sales tax to the City. HdL audit fees are contingent on finding revenue, with
the fees based on a percentage of sales tax recovered. The recovery varies each year
based on these audits, as do the audit fees. Audit fees are only charged if additional
sales tax is recovered. As sales tax recovery occurs, the additional revenue and offset
of audit fees will be budgeted.

DISCUSSION

HdL provides sales, use, and transaction tax expertise, analysis, recaptured revenues,
and precise revenue projections for the City’s general sales tax and Measure AV sales
tax. Staff recommend that the City continue its relationship with HdL for these services.

1.1  The City hereby engages CONSULTANT, and CONSULTANT accepts such

1. Sales and Use Tax and Economic Analysis/Forecasting Services/Reports

1.1. CONSULTANT will establish a special database identifying the name, address,
and quarterly allocations of all sales tax producers within the City. This database will
be utilized to generate special reports to the City on major sales tax producers by
rank and category, sales tax activity by categories, or business districts, identification

statewide sales.

that will be monitored and corrected include but are not limited to transposition errors
resulting in misallocations; erroneous consolidation of multiple outlets; formula errors;
misreporting of “point of sale” to the wrong location; delays in reporting new outlets;
misallocating use tax payments to the allocation pools or wrong jurisdiction; and
erroneous fund transfers and adjustments.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8901 with Pro West and Associates, Inc., to provide
  Geographic Information System Services in a not to exceed amount of $300,000
  for a three-year term; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute the Agreement No. A-
  8901 with Pro West and Associates, Inc., including minimal and/or non-
  substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The City’s Geographical Information Systems (GIS) Program provides City staff with a
toolset to view parcel and data layers within Palmdale City boundaries. Some of the
tools include application viewers to access parcel information, customized applications
for the field staff to track inventory, customized maps, and reporting. The City contracted
with Pro West for GIS services for a one-year term. During this time, the City migrated
to a more cutting-edge and industry-leading Esri ArcGIS software and implemented
improvements that benefit the organization and community.

DISCUSSION

The current agreement with Pro West and Associates, Inc. expires on June 30, 2024.
Staff are pleased with the services provided by Pro West and recommend that the City
Council approve a new agreement for a term of three (3) years. This will allow for

of the document was necessary to stay current with best practices, to provide a clear
and concise Salary and Benefits policy, and to allow for simplified implementation and
distribution of the policy.

DISCUSSION

Staff proposes the adoption of a stand-alone Salary and Benefits Policy. This policy
contains information on holidays, accrued leave (vacation time, sick leave, etc.), leaves
of absence, and related issues and ensures compliance with all applicable laws. It is
standard practice to update this policy annually or at such times that legislation requires
an update.

Salary and Benefits are key components of the City’s strategic plan to attract and retain
talent. A dedicated policy underscores the importance of these elements and highlights
the City’s commitment to offering compelling and comprehensive packages.

  The Deputy Director in Human Resources shall ascertain and record the duties

consist of classes of positions defined by class specifications and job title. The
classification plan shall be developed and maintained so that all positions with
substantially similar duties, responsibilities, authority, and character of work are
included within the same classification and that similar schedules of compensation
apply to all positions in the same classification.

  The appointing authority may revise the classification plan whenever he or she
deems necessary, contingent upon approval by the City Council.

  Following the adoption of the classification plan, the Deputy Director in Human

appointing authority.

  Except as directed by the appointing authority, no person shall be appointed or
employed to fill a new position until the classification plan is amended to add the new
position.

Section 2-5 - Reclassification
  If the duties of a position change materially such that the position belongs in a
different classification, Human Resources will review the position and if appropriate,
recommend to the City Manager and reallocate the position to the appropriate
classification contingent on approval by City Council.

  The title of the classification to which any position is allocated shall be used in all

departmental policy.

prohibited by City policy and California state law.
  An employee who returns to work for the City within one year of separation of
service will be credited with up to forty (40) hours of sick leave. If the employee
separated with less than forty (40) hours of accrued sick leave, then he/she will be
credited with the number of hours he/she had accrued at the time of separation.
  If an employee has accrued sick leave in their bank, it must be used.
Employees cannot voluntarily go in unpaid status.  If an employee’s sick leave is
exhausted, other accrued leave may be used at the discretion of the department with
Human Resources approval.

Section 4-4 - Payment and Conversion of Accumulated Sick Leave

  Full-time and benefited part-time employees may be entitled to convert either 20
or 40 hours of sick leave to an equal amount of vacation time or pay during September.
In order to be entitled to convert, the employee must have at least 212 hours of
accumulated sick leave at the time of the annual request, and must have at least 192
hours of accumulated sick leave after the conversion during the last pay period in
September.
  An employee whose employment with the City terminates or is terminated before
the last day of the last pay period in September is not eligible to convert sick leave,
including on a prorated basis.

Section 4-5 - Jury Duty
  Full-time and benefited part-time employees who have received a summons for
jury duty during their normal working hours shall be deemed on duty and shall receive
their regular pay for up to a maximum of ten (10) calendar days of jury service. In some
circumstances, exempt employees may be required to be compensated beyond ten
days under the provisions of state or federal law.
  An employee who volunteers for jury duty, or who serves on a grand jury, will not
  _______________________
  Updated and Rev. 06/2024
  16
 be paid for that time by the City.
  If an employee is required to serve on jury duty, the employee must notify his or
her supervisor of the need for time off for jury duty as soon as a notice or summons
from the court is received. An employee must present a verification from the court clerk
of having served on jury duty in order to qualify for pay. Employees will be expected to
report or return to work for the remainder of their work schedule on any day they are
dismissed from jury duty. Employees shall maintain their normal work schedule and
may not alter their work schedule and/or flex their time off while serving on jury duty.
  Employees who are scheduled to work a night shift assignment are not required
to report or return to work on a day they report to jury duty. Employees working the
night shift should contact Human Resources for specific assistance in coordinating jury
duty with their schedule.

Section 4-6 - Other Court Appearances
  Any employee who is called as a witness in a trial, deposition or other legal
proceeding, arising out of or related to the course of his or her employment, shall be
deemed to be on duty and shall receive pay for the time so engaged. An employee
absent as a witness for a non-job related purpose shall not be entitled to pay during
such absence. Exceptions to this rule can only be made on the written authorization of
the appointing authority. Employees may request such an exception by submitting the
appropriate form to the City Attorney’s office, prior to the required appearance. In some
circumstances, exempt employees may be required to be compensated under the
provisions of state or federal law when absent as a witness for a non-job-related
purpose.

Section 4-7 - Bereavement/Reproductive Loss Leave
  Full-time and benefited part-time employees are permitted to take five (5) days
leave upon the occurrence of a qualifying death or reproductive loss event.
Bereavement leave may be taken if the employee’s absence from work is necessitated
by the death of a member of the employee’s Immediate Family. Full-Time employees
shall receive up to three (3) paid days for bereavement. Benefited Part-Time employees
receive Bereavement Leave on a prorated basis. If an employee has exhausted paid
bereavement leave, the employee may use other available leave time, such as sick
leave or other compensatory time off. Such paid sick leave (or other compensatory time
  _______________________
  Updated and Rev. 06/2024
  17
 off) will run concurrently with leave taken pursuant to this section.
  Qualifying death definition: Immediate family shall be defined as the death of an
employee’s spouse, domestic partner, child, stepchild, parent, parent-in-law,
grandparent, grandchild, brother, sister, mother/father-in-law, son or daughter-in-law,
brother or sister-in-law, legal guardian, or custodial child, or the same relatives of a
domestic partner, any relative by blood or marriage who is a member of the employee’s
household, domestic partner, and any parent, grandparent, spouse, child, brother or
sister of the employee, or the parent, brother or sister of the employee’s spouse, ex-
spouse, or deceased spouse, regardless of residence or employee’s current marital
status.
  Reproductive loss definition: any failed adoption, failed surrogacy, miscarriage,
stillbirth or unsuccessful assisted reproduction by the employee, the employee’s current
spouse or domestic partner, or by another individual if the employee would have been a
parent of a child had the reproductive loss not occurred.
  Bereavement/Reproductive Loss leave may be taken on non-consecutive days
but must be completed within three (3) months of the date of death or reproductive loss.
  For leave related to a reproductive loss, employees may take multiple leaves for
subsequent reproductive losses. However, employees are limited to a total of twenty
(20) days of reproductive loss leave in a twelve (12) month period. Further, employees
receive three (3) paid days of reproductive loss leave each calendar year. If an
employee has exhausted this paid reproductive loss leave, the employee may use other
available leave time, such as sick leave or other compensatory time off, for a
subsequent reproductive loss. Such paid sick leave (or other compensatory time off) will
run concurrently with leave taken pursuant to this section.
  Employees will be required to provide documentation of the death of the
qualifying family member within 30 days of the first day of leave. Documentation
includes, but is not limited to: a death certificate, a published obituary, or written
verification of death, burial or memorial services from a mortuary, funeral home, burial
society, crematorium, religious institution or governmental agency.
  Employees will not be required to provide documentation of a reproductive loss
and City will not request documentation.

Section 4-8 - Time for Voting
  Employees who do not have sufficient time outside of their regular working hours
  _______________________

  18
 to vote in a statewide election may request time off to vote from his/her supervisor. If
possible, employees should make their request at least two (2) days in advance of the
election. Up to two hours of paid time off will be provided at the beginning or end of the
employee's regular shift, whichever will allow the most free time for voting and the least
time off work.

Section 4-9 Relay Appointment
  The Appointing Authority may, without specific City Council approval to amend
the Authorized Full-Time List, permit the simultaneous appointment of two employees to
one budgeted position within the Classified Service to allow for an employee departing
from that position to train an employee newly appointed to that position. Such “relay
appointment” can be made only where the departing employee has provided the City
with a written and irrevocable notice of retirement or resignation. A relay appointment
may not exceed 60 days.

SECTION 5 - OTHER TIME OFF

Section 5-1 - Time Off To Attend School Activities
  An employee who is a parent, guardian or grandparent with custody of a child in
kindergarten or grades 1-12, inclusive, or attending a licensed child day care facility,
who wishes to take time off to participate in activities of the school or child care facility,
may take off up to eight (8) hours each calendar month (up to a maximum of forty (40)
hours each school year), per child. The employee must give reasonable notice to his or
her supervisor of the planned absence and use existing vacation, administrative leave,
compensatory time or floating holiday accrued for this purpose. Otherwise, such time
off for nonexempt employees is unpaid. For exempt employees, such time off may be
paid or unpaid as provided by applicable law. The City requires documentation from the
school noting the date and time of the employee’s visit.
  If both parents of a child work for the City, only one parent (the first to provide
notice) may take the time off unless the City approves both parents taking time off
simultaneously.
  An employee may also be granted time off to attend a school conference
involving the possible suspension of his or her child.

 Section 5-2 - Leave Related To Domestic Violence or Sexual Assault
  Leave for Victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault, Stalking or Other
Crimes to Obtain Restraining Orders or Injunctive Relief: Any employee who is a victim
of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or other crime may take leave from work
to obtain or attempt to obtain any relief, including, but not limited to: a temporary
restraining order, restraining order, or other injunctive relief to help ensure the health,
safety, or welfare of the employee or their child, if the employee provides advance
notice of the need for leave. If advance notice is not feasible, the employee must
provide any of the following certifications within a reasonable time after the leave: a
police report indicating that the employee was a victim; a court order protecting the
employee from the perpetrator; evidence from the district attorney or court that the
employee has appeared in court; or documentation from a health care provider or
counselor that the employee was undergoing treatment for physical or mental injuries or
abuse. The leave is unpaid unless the employee elects to use Healthy Workplace
Healthy Family Act of 2014 sick leave, accrued vacation or paid leave, or other
compensatory time off.

  Leave for Victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault, Stalking or Other
Crimes to Obtain Medical Attention or Counseling or Safety Planning: Any employee
who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or other crime, may take
leave from work to attend to any of the following: obtaining medical attention or
psychological counseling; obtaining services from a shelter, program or crisis center; or
participating in safety planning or other actions to increase safety, if the employee
provides advance notice of the employee’s intention to take time off for these purposes.
If advance notice is not feasible, the employee must provide any of the following to the
City within a reasonable time after the leave: a police report indicating that the
employee was a victim; a court order protecting the employee from the perpetrator;
evidence from the district attorney or court that the employee has appeared in court; or
documentation from a health care provider or counselor that the employee was
undergoing treatment for physical or mental injuries or abuse. The leave is unpaid
unless the employee elects to use Healthy Workplace Healthy Family Act of 2014 sick
leave, accrued vacation or personal leave, or compensatory time off.

 Section 5-3 - Crime Victims' Leave
  The City will provide unpaid time off to an employee to attend judicial
proceedings related to a crime, if that employee is a victim of crime, an immediate
family member (as defined by law) of a victim, a registered domestic partner of a victim,
or the child of a registered domestic partner of a victim. The City requires that where
feasible, in advance of taking leave, the employee provide Human Resources with a
copy of the notice of each scheduled proceeding that is provided to the victim by the
agency responsible for providing notice. If advance notice is not possible, the employee
is required to provide Human Resources with a copy of the notice within a reasonable
time. Employees may use existing vacation, administrative leave, compensatory time or
floating holiday accrued hours for this purpose. Otherwise, such time off for nonexempt
employees is unpaid. For exempt employees, such time off may be paid or unpaid as
provided by applicable law.  If an employee is a victim of a crime and is called to
testify in a legal proceeding, the employee may be paid in accordance with the benefits
provided for in the section herein entitled “Other Court Appearances.”

Section 5-4 - Other Time Off
  The City will grant other time off as required by law. The employee will provide
reasonable advance notice and written verification of the need for such time off. If time
off is taken due to an emergency the employee within a reasonable amount of time will
provide appropriate verification as required by the City.

SECTION 6 - LEAVES OF ABSENCE

Section 6-1 - General Provisions
  The appointing authority may grant a leave of absence in certain circumstances.
An employee is required to notify his or her supervisor and Human Resources in writing
as soon as he or she becomes aware of a need for a leave of absence. The appointing
authority will consider the request in accordance with applicable law and the City's leave
policies. An employee will be notified whether the leave request is granted or denied. If
an employee is granted leave, he or she must comply with the terms and conditions of
the leave including keeping in touch with his or her supervisor and Human Resources
during the leave and giving prompt notice if there is any change in the return date.
  In most circumstances an employee must not accept other employment or apply

  _______________________
  Updated and Rev. 06/2024
  21
 for unemployment insurance while on a leave of absence. Acceptance of other
employment while on leave may be treated as a voluntary resignation from employment
at the City. Misuse of a leave of absence is also prohibited. Misuse of leave includes
not returning to work from a leave when the reason the leave was granted no longer
exists and using leave for a purpose for which it was not granted. For instance, if an
employee is granted leave for two weeks to take care of an ill family member but the
employee goes on vacation, or after one week the family member is no longer ill and the
employee fails to return to work, the employee has misused the leave.
  Benefits, such as vacation and paid sick leave, will not accrue during the unpaid
portion of any leave of absence. Except as otherwise provided herein, or by law, upon
timely return from a leave of absence, an employee will be credited with the full
employment status that existed prior to the start of the leave. An employee will not
receive credit for the time he or she was on leave during the unpaid portion of any
leave, except that the employee will retain his or her original date of hire.
  If an employee does not return to work from the leave prior to or immediately
upon the expiration of the leave granted by the appointing authority, the employee will
not be reinstated to employment with the City and will be considered to have voluntarily
resigned from employment, unless the employee has requested and been granted an
extension of leave, or additional leave. Any request for an extension of leave or for
additional leave must be made in writing prior to the original expiration of the leave. Any
such request received after the original expiration of leave will not be granted. The
appointing authority may refuse to grant an extension or request for additional leave in
its sole discretion except as otherwise provided by law.
  The City will not continue to pay for the premiums for group health insurance for
employees or their eligible dependents during the time the employee is on a leave of
absence except as required herein, or by law. Prior to starting any leave of absence an
employee must make all necessary arrangements with Human Resources to pay the
required insurance premiums.  An employee's failure to make the required
arrangements may result in loss of insurance coverage for the employee and
dependents.
  Depending on the circumstances described in this Salary and Benefits Policy, an
employee is required to use, or may elect to use, and in one circumstance an employee
is prohibited from using, accrued paid sick and vacation leave, and other accrued paid
leaves (floating holidays, compensatory time, and administrative leave) during the
  _______________________
  Updated and Rev. 06/2024
  22
 otherwise unpaid portion of the leave of absence.
  Any sick, vacation or other accrued leave payments made to an employee will be
integrated with any wage replacement benefits (such as workers’ compensation and
disability insurance wage replacement benefits) an employee receives, so that the sum
of wage replacement benefits and accrued leave benefits an employee receives while
on a leave of absence will not be more than his or her regular compensation if the
employee was not on leave.
  “Regular compensation” for an exempt employee means the employee’s weekly
salary and for a nonexempt employee means the employee’s hourly rate times the
number of straight time hours normally worked by the employee during the workweek.
  Any employee on leave is required to notify promptly Human Resources upon
receipt of all checks for wage replacement benefits such as workers' compensation or
disability insurance wage replacement benefits. The employee must also promptly send
a copy of the checks to Human Resources and provide Human Resources any other
information or documents requested. Once Human Resources receives and processes
the required and requested documents and notifications, the employee will be paid the
amount of sick, vacation, or other paid accrued leave that will result in the employee
receiving the amount of regular compensation that the employee received before the
leave of absence, but no more.
  The payment of accrued paid leaves by the City will reduce the amount of such
accumulated leave available to the employee by the amount of leave paid, converted
into hours based upon the regular straight time hourly rate then paid to a nonexempt
employee. For an exempt employee, the conversion will be based upon an hourly rate
calculated by dividing the employee’s weekly salary by forty.
  The City’s payments of accrued paid leaves to an employee on leave will be
made in arrears on the City’s established pay dates, and such payments are subject to
verification by the City of whether the employee did or did not receive wage
replacement benefits.
  The City's leave of absence policies are not intended to conflict with applicable
law. If there should be any conflict between these policies and the provisions of
applicable law, those laws are controlling over these policies.

Section 6-3 - Pregnancy Disability Leave
1.  An employee who is disabled because of pregnancy, childbirth, or a related
  medical condition is entitled to an unpaid leave for up to the number of hours she
  would normally work within four calendar months (one-third of a year or 17 1/3
  weeks). For a full-time employee who works 40 hours per week, “four months”
  means 693 hours of leave entitlement, based on 40 hour per week times 17 1/3
  weeks. An employee who works less than 40 hours per week will receive a pro
  rata or proportional amount of leave.

  A.  Notice: Requests for pregnancy disability leave must be submitted in
  writing with reasonable advance notice of the medical need for the leave.
  All leaves must be confirmed in writing, have an agreed-upon specific date
  of return, and be submitted to City’s Human Resources department.

  B.  Certification: The request for pregnancy disability leave must be supported
  by a written certification from the attending physician stating that: (1) the
  employee is disabled from working by pregnancy, childbirth or a related
  medical condition; (2) the date on which the employee became disabled
  by pregnancy, childbirth or a related medical condition; and (3) the
  estimated duration or end date of the leave.

  C.  Compensation during Leave: Pregnancy disability leaves are without pay.
  However, the employee must first use sick leave, if any. Once sick leave is
  depleted, the employee may elect to use vacation leave or any other
  accrued paid time off during the leave.

  D.  Benefits during Leave: Group Health Insurance:
  i.  Group Health Insurance: An employee on pregnancy disability
  leave may continue to receive any group health insurance coverage
  that was provided before her leave, beginning on the date the
  pregnancy disability leave begins and continuing for up to four
  _______________________
  Updated and Rev. 06/2024
  40
   months in a 12-month period, at the same level and under the
  same conditions that coverage would have been provided if the
  employee had continued in employment continuously for the
  duration of the leave. The City may recover premiums it paid to
  maintain health coverage if an employee does not return to work
  following pregnancy disability leave, unless the reason for the
  failure to return is a circumstance beyond her control or the use of
  the separate right to 12 weeks of bonding leave under the FMLA.

  ii.  Sick, Administrative and Vacation Leaves: Sick, administrative and
  vacation leaves do not accrue while an employee is on unpaid
  pregnancy disability leave.

  iii.  Employee Status during Leave: The employee retains employee
  status during the leave. The leave is not a break in service for
  purposes of longevity or seniority under any collective bargaining
  agreement or employee benefit plan. Benefits will be resumed upon
  the employee’s reinstatement in the same manner and at the same
  levels as provided when the leave began, without any new
  qualification period, physical exam, or other qualifying provisions.

E.  In accordance with the Family Care and Medical Leave Policy, pregnancy
  leave runs concurrently with FMLA.

F.  Reinstatement:
  i.  Upon the expiration of pregnancy leave, the employee will be

  not eliminated for a legitimate business reason during the leave.

  ii.  If the employee’s original position is no longer available, the

  iii.  If upon return from leave an employee is unable to perform the
  essential functions of her job because of a physical or mental

   disability, the City will initiate an interactive process with the

Upon return from such leave the employee shall submit to the appointing authority a

Section 6-4 - Military Leave

Military leave will be granted in accordance with federal and state law. An employee
requesting leave for this purpose shall promptly provide the City with a copy of the
military orders specifying the dates, site and purpose of the activity or mission. Within
the limits of such orders, the City may determine when the leave is to be taken and may
modify the employee’s work schedule to accommodate the request for leave.

Section 6-5 - Benefits Earned During A Leave of Absence Without Pay
  An employee on leave of absence without pay shall not earn vacation, holidays,
sick leave or administrative leave. Subject to the terms of the group health insurance
plans, an employee on a leave of absence without pay may continue to participate in all
group insurance plans upon the approval of the appointing authority provided the
employee pays the entire premium for the insurance(s) plan(s) except where otherwise
required by law or by these policies. Insurance premiums must be paid in advance.
Arrangements for insurance continuation must be made prior to the start of the leave of
absence.

SECTION 8 - EXEMPT EMPLOYEES

Section 8-1 - Exempt Employees
  Work hours for exempt employees, such as directors and exempt employees, are
such as are necessary for completing their duties in a timely and efficient manner
including, but not limited to, attendance at all meetings as directed by the City Manager,
supervision of employees, coordination of office and City activities, consultation with the
City Manager and/or other employees and providing service to the public.
  Generally speaking, exempt employees should expect to be at work for all hours
that his or her respective offices or work sites are open.
  The City recognizes the benefit and need to foster and maintain a strong,
professional administrative team. The appointing authority has the discretion to

 designate exempt employees in accordance with applicable state and federal law.

goals and objectives to meet community needs regardless of the length of the workday
or workweek and are exempt from the overtime pay requirements of applicable law.
The terms of this section and the exempt salary and leave plan shall apply to only those
exempt employees specifically designated by the appointing authority.

Section 8-2 - Exempt Employee Compensation
  The appointing authority shall have the sole discretion to determine the level of
compensation paid to exempt employees. The placement, advancement or reduction of
an individual within the salary range or salary level shall be determined only after a
review by the appointing authority to determine the extent to which the exempt
employee has met the expectations and objectives of his or her respective job. The
appointing authority also shall consider the degree to which an exempt employee has
been of positive value to the effectiveness of the City's administrative team. An exempt
employee’s current salary or a salary advancement shall be neither automatic nor a
matter of right, but based solely upon merit and performance.

  Except as to Director/Executive Management employees, employees the City
classified as exempt on or before August 3, 2011, accrue administrative leave bi-weekly
at the rate of 96 hours each fiscal year; and employees the City classified as exempt
after August 3, 2011, accrue administrative leave bi-weekly at the rate 80 hours each
fiscal year. Pursuant to Resolution 2023-037, all Director/Executive Management
employees accrue administrative leave at the rate of 3.7 hours per pay period (96 hours
annually).

an employee is on paid leave).
  An employee who the City classified as exempt on or before August 1, 2012,
accumulates administrative leave without limit. An employee who the City classified as
exempt after August 1, 2012, can accumulate a maximum of 240 hours of administrative
leave. Once this maximum amount is accumulated, the employee ceases accruing any
additional administrative leave. An employee resumes accruing administrative leave

  AMOUNT OF $222,300 FOR A TERM OF NINE MONTHS

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8892, with Transtech Engineers, Inc., for Acting City
  Engineer and Traffic Engineer staff augmentation support services in the amount
  of $222,300 for a term of nine months; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8892,
  with Transtech Engineers, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantive
  changes.

BACKGROUND

In April 2024, the City Engineer retired. The City is currently taking measures to recruit a
replacement for this position. The City Engineer is a key position that reviews and
approves all the design and construction plans/activities, all the engineering standards
and sets development conditions. It is not unusual for the recruitment of such a position
to take several months.

DISCUSSION

In the interim, to address this vacancy and continue meeting City objectives, the City
worked with several firms to find a qualified candidate. Transtech Engineers, Inc. is a
multi-disciplinary consulting firm providing municipal services to public agencies and cities
since 1989. One of the unique qualifications of Transtech Engineers, Inc. is that they
serve several public agencies as municipal contract service providers, including, but not
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Agreement A-8892 with Transtech Engineers, Inc.
June 26, 2024

limited to acting as the Contract City Engineer, City Traffic Engineer, CIP Manager, PW
Director. They were able to provide a list of qualified and available engineers to act as the
Acting City and Traffic Engineer. City staff interviewed the potential candidates and
requested a proposal for services from Transtech Engineers, Inc.

The proposed terms of the contract include:

    Providing City Engineering services for an average of 20 hours a week (both
  remote and in-person);
    Providing Traffic Engineering services for an average of 5-10 hours per week (both
  remote and in-person); and,
    Nine-month term with a total fee not to exceed $222,300.

FISCAL IMPACT

$222,300; The City will utilize cost savings resulting from the vacancy of these positions
to finance temporary staff until the positions are filled. Funds have been allocated and are
available in the Salary and Benefit accounts for Fiscal Year 2024 and are also included
in the proposed Fiscal Year 2025 operating budget.

  WHEREAS, Section 13307 of the Elections Code of the State of California
provides that the governing body of any local agency adopt regulations pertaining
to materials prepared by any candidate for a municipal election, including costs of
the candidate’s statement;

NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE, DOES
HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS. That pursuant to Section 13307 of
the Elections Code of the State of California, each candidate for elective office to
be voted for at an Election to be held in the City of Palmdale on Tuesday,
November 5, 2024, may prepare a candidate statement on an appropriate form
provided by the City Clerk. The statement may include the name, age, and
occupation of the candidate and a brief description of no more than 200 words of
the candidate’s education and qualifications expressed by the candidate himself
or herself. The statement shall not include party affiliation of the candidate nor
membership or activity in partisan political organizations. The statement shall be
in typewritten form and filed with the City Clerk at the time the candidate’s
nomination papers are filed. Except as provided in Election Code Section 13309,
the statement may be withdrawn, but not changed, during the period for filing
nomination papers and until 5:00 p.m. of the next working day after the close of
the nomination period.

  SECTION 2. FOREIGN LANGUAGE POLICY.

  A. Pursuant to the Federal Voting Rights Act, candidate statements
  will be translated into all languages required by the County of Los
  Angeles. The County is required to translate candidate
  statements into the following languages:

  Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, Tagalog/Filipino, Vietnamese,
  Korean, Cambodian/Khmer, Hindi, Thai, Armenian, Farsi,

  Bengali, Burmese, Gujarati, Indonesian, Mongolian, Telugu and
  Russian.

  The County of Los Angeles will print and mail sample ballots and
  candidate statements in the required languages to only those
  voters who are on the county voter file as having requested a
  sample ballot in a particular language. The County will make the
  sample ballots and candidate statements in the required
  languages available at vote centers, on the County’s website, and
  in the City’s Election Official’s office.

  SECTION 3. PAYMENT.

  A. Translations:

  1. The candidate shall not be required to pay for the cost, if any,
  of translating the candidate statements into any required
  foreign language as specified in (A) and/or (B) of Section 2
  above pursuant to Federal and/or State law.

  2. The candidate shall be required to pay for the cost of
  translating the candidate’s statement into any foreign
  language that is not required as specified in (A) and/or (B) of
  Section 2 above, pursuant to Federal and/or State law, but is
  requested as an option by the candidate.

  1. The candidate shall be required to pay for the cost of printing

  pamphlet.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement A-8794 with Konica Minolta Business Solutions USA, Inc. for
  document imaging and indexing services for a not to exceed amount of $681,120
  for a term of three (3) years with the option to extend for two additional terms of
  one (1) year each, and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8794
  with Konica Minolta Business Solutions USA, Inc., including any minimal and/or
  non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND

To align the City’s storing of permanent records with best practices for records
management, staff was directed to research options that would image plans/records to
include ease of preserving long-term and permanent records, reduce the demand for
physical storage space, and increase the accessibility of records through the City’s
Electronic Document Management System (EDMS).

DISCUSSION

On November 7, 2023, staff released Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 23-001-1200;
Document Imaging and Indexing, on Planet Bids. The RFP closed on December 11, 2023,
and received eight responses. A team of City staff from various departments evaluated
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Agrmt No. A-8794 with Konica Minolta Business Solutions U.S.A., Inc.
June 26, 2024
Page 2

the proposals, and the top three respondents were interviewed: Konica Minolta,
Metasource, and ARC. Based on the interviews, Konica Minolta best met the City’s
requirements.

Konica Minolta strongly understood the City’s goal of preserving long-term and permanent
records electronically. Many of these records are decades old. This project will ensure an
electronic version of these records before they deteriorate, which is critical. Konica
Minolta will image 3,000 multi-page plans and more than 3,500 boxes of records. The
imaged documents will be uploaded into our EDMS, Evolve. They will be easily
accessible and will allow the City to provide records to the public in a timely manner.

As the project progresses, the City will also benefit from improved efficiencies and cost
savings. Retrievals and public record requests can be searched for and provided
electronically, saving staff time, labor, material, and postage costs. In addition, the
physical storage space required to house records will be greatly decreased, eliminating
the need for a 7,000-square-foot warehouse and potentially allowing for the sale or
repurposing of the warehouse.

$681,120; Funds are budgeted and available in FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25. Funding for
subsequent years will be proposed through the annual budget process.

 On March 11, 2021, the American Rescue Plan Act (“ARP Act”) was signed into law.
The ARP Act was intended to provide increased aid to individuals, families,
businesses, and governments affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The ARP Act
established and funded the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (the
“CSLFRF”), which included two hundred forty (240) billion dollars for state, territorial,
local, and Tribal governments that are being used to fight the pandemic and
accelerate local economic recovery.

MANDATORY CONTRACT PROVISIONS FOR ARP ACT EXPENDITURES:
Procurement processes for expenditures using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
funds generally follow state and local rules. In most cases, city procurement policies
will satisfy the federal requirements. One notable difference is that federal
procurement regulations mandate specific contract provisions in certain
circumstances. There are no requirements for contracts or expenditures of less than
$10,000. However, using ARPA funds for contracts in excess of $10,000 triggers the
mandatory contract provisions in 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix II.

Most contract provisions are required only on those exceeding $100,000 or those for
construction projects of any amount. However, mandatory contract provisions will
apply if a city obligates ARPA funds to a contract that exceeds $100,000.

For ease of administration, below is an explanation of the mandatory contract
provisions and model language necessary for compliance with federal law
disclosures.

2 C.F.R. PART 200: APPENDIX II, CONTRACT PROVISIONS

  • For contracts over $10,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  termination for cause and convenience by the local government, including the
  process for termination and the basis for settlement.
  • For contracts over $100,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  administrative, contractual, or legal remedies if a contractor violates or
  breaches the contract, including sanctions and penalties for the breach.
  • In accepting the ARPA award, local governments agreed to include an EEO
  statement in any federally assisted construction contract defined in 41 CFR
  Part 60-1.3. A federally assisted construction contract is defined as follows:
  o Any agreement or modification thereof between any applicant and a
  person for construction work which is paid for in whole or in part with
  funds obtained from the government or borrowed on the credit of the
  government pursuant to any federal program involving a grant, contract,
  loan, insurance, or guarantee, or undertaken pursuant to any federal
  program involving such grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee,
  or any application or modification thereof approved by the government
  for a grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee under which the
  applicant itself participates in the construction work.

wages to be paid are those determined by the State Director of the Department of
Industrial Relations. Section 1776 requires the Contractor and all subcontractors to
keep accurate payroll records, specifies the contents thereof, their inspection and
duplication procedures and certain notices required of the Contractor pertaining to
their location.

8.  Section 1777.5 of the Labor Code requires Contractor or subcontractor
employing workers in any apprenticeable occupation to apply to the Joint
Apprenticeship Committee nearest the site of the public works project, which
administers the apprenticeship program in that trade for a certificate of approval. The
certificate will also fix the ratio of apprentices to journeymen to be used in the
performance of the Contract. The Contractor is required to make contributions to
funds established for the administration of apprenticeship programs if he employs
registered apprentices or journeymen in any apprenticeable trade and if other
contractors on the public works site are making such contributions. Information
relative to apprenticeship standards, contributions, wage schedules and other
requirements may be obtained from the State Director of Industrial Relations or from
the Division of Apprenticeship Standards. Section 1777.6 of the Labor Code provides
that it shall be unlawful to refuse to accept otherwise qualified employees as
registered apprentices solely on the grounds of race, religious creed, color, national
origin, ancestry, sex, or age.

9.  Eight hours labor constitutes a legal day's work, as set forth in Labor Code
Section 1810. The statutory provisions for penalties for failure to comply with the
State's wage and hour laws will be enforced as set forth in Labor Code Section 1813.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or designee to bind
insurance coverage as anticipated in the budget annually for the approved legislative
bodies.

BACKGROUND

Each year, the City responds to applications for various types of insurance and provides
those applications to the selected insurance broker. The broker engages with the
appropriate insurers to obtain proposals that best fit the City's needs. The proposals are
then provided to the City and, if accepted, bound by the City Manager. Proposals include,
but are not limited to, different types of coverage, special coverage needs based on new
business, and self-insured retentions. The City is part of a self-insured pool that
specializes in public entity coverage with similar exposures. This has historically provided
cost savings because the risk is shared amongst other agencies.

DISCUSSION

Staff requests that the City Council authorize the City Manager to bind insurance
coverage, via the attached resolution, for the City of Palmdale, the Successor Agency to
the Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Palmdale, the Palmdale Civic
Authority, the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale, the Industrial Development
Authority of the City of Palmdale, the Palmdale Airport Authority, the Palmdale Financing
Authority, (hereinafter collectively referred to as “each entity”), annually, to include but not
be limited to general liability, property, workers' compensation, automobile, and other
necessary insurance policies. This will ensure there is no lapse in coverage. Costs are
based on market conditions and whether the City chooses to increase or decrease
coverage or coverage types.

FISCAL IMPACT

Insurance payments will vary depending on factors such as the insurance market,
actuarial history, number of participants in the self-insured pool program, increase in City
assets, and the need to purchase additional policies.

Estimated dollar amounts will be included in the annual budget for each corresponding
fiscal year.

  Industrial Development Authority of the City of Palmdale, the Palmdale Airport

  Community Foundation.

  and regulations.

C. The City Manager shall report to the City Council on the details of the insurance
  coverage bound, including costs, coverage limits, and terms, at least annually or as
  requested by the City Council.

  SECTION 4. Effective Date: This resolution shall take effect immediately upon
its adoption.

  SECTION 5. Duration: This resolution shall remain in effect until repealed by City
Council.

BACKGROUND

Each year the City is required to adopt a budget for its operation. The budget serves as
the City’s financial plan for the Fiscal Year beginning July 1 through June 30. It defines
City priorities for the provision of services to the community.

According to the Palmdale Municipal Code: Chapter 3.04 Budget Adoption Procedures,
the City Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May
31 of each year. The proposed budget was brought before the City Council on May 17,
2023. Additionally, the City Council shall conduct a public hearing on the proposed budget
before adoption and shall adopt a budget prescribing the spending policy of the City for
the ensuing fiscal year on or before the thirtieth day of June of each year.

Revenues
Estimating revenues for the upcoming fiscal year and forecasting out-years is essential
to the budget development process. Revenue projections are formed by analyzing prior
year actual receipts, trends, new revenue sources, grant opportunities, fees for services,
and State economic outlook. Citywide revenues are estimated to be $528.45 million.

The City’s General Fund is the largest unrestricted funding source, with a total of $117.2
million in projected resources. General Fund resources include property tax, sales tax,
other taxes, fees, and charges for service. Measure AV is a general sales and use tax
that, although not required, the City presents separately from the General Fund for
transparency purposes. Measure AV has a total of $22.8 million in projected resources
projected in Fiscal Year 2024-25.

Operating Appropriations
The proposed operating budget for all funds is $567.5 million citywide, and the General
Fund operating budget is proposed to be $123.5 million. The supporting schedules
provide additional details on appropriations.

Intent of the Approving Legislative Bodies:

  1. In accordance with the City of Palmdale Municipal Code Section 3.04.020, the City
  Manager shall submit a proposed budget to the City Council no later than May 31st
  of each year; and,

  2. The City Manager has submitted a proposed budget to the Approving Legislative
  Bodies for the Fiscal Year 2024-25 for review, consideration and adoption; and,

  3. The City Council has caused a public hearing to be held on said budget, as
  amended, on June 26, 2024, with public notice of the hearing published at least
  fourteen (14) days prior to said hearing, has further considered the proposed
  budget, and has made revisions therein; and,

  4. Section 2.04.060 and 3.04.101 of the Palmdale Municipal Code require that the
  City Manager oversee and accomplish, with the professional staffs assistance, a
  budget prescribing the spending policy of the City for the ensuing fiscal year be
  adopted on or before the thirtieth day of June each year; and,

  5. After consideration and analysis, the Approving Legislative Bodies, each
  separately, find it is in the interest of the health, welfare and safety of the City and
  each entity, its citizens and businesspersons, to adopt the financial plan within the
  budget for the receipt and expenditure of public monies in Fiscal Year 2024-25;
  and,

  6. The City Council has approved a General Fund Operating Reserve Policy of 20%

 SAVING RESIDENTS MONEY
The City of Palmdale is dedicated to completing projects while saving you money.
Here are a few of the ways we are saving taxpayers’ dollars:

  Long-term Financial Planning
  The City is committed to long-term comprehensive financial planning. It
  prepares and publicly presents, during the budget process, a detailed five-
  year forecast that includes an analysis of key revenues and expenditures,
  along with proposed measures to address any projected gaps.

  Pension Stabilization Trust Fund
  CalPERS: The City has taken many proactive steps to manage rising pension
  costs through the years. The most significant recent action was to allocate
  $1.25 million to the Pension Stabilization Trust Fund, which now has over
  $9.4 million reserved for future Unfunded Actuarial Liability (UAL) payments.

  Grant Funding
  The City applies for and receives grants from a variety of sources at the local,
  state and federal levels. The funds received will go toward many citywide
  projects including Palmdale Blvd./R-14 interchange improvements, arterial road
  rehabilitation projects, Courson Park revitalization, housing development and
  rehabilitation projects, Avenue R signal synchronization, Rancho Vista Blvd./
  Sierra Hwy. grade separation and more.

 About the City of Palmdale
The City of Palmdale, with nearly 170,000 residents, sits perfectly nestled in the Antelope Valley
against the picturesque backdrop of the San Gabriel Mountains. Our community thrives on its
forward-thinking and innovative ethos, driving progress across various sectors, from transportation
to aerospace to public safety. Families enjoy Palmdale’s excellent schools, affordable housing,
abundant recreational opportunities, diverse local culture and welcoming atmosphere, all within
reach of the Los Angeles metropolitan area. Despite its urban proximity, Palmdale retains its
identity as a desert oasis, boasting stunning landscapes, native Joshua trees and over 300 days of
annual sunshine. Explore further at www.CityOfPalmdaleCA.gov.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2024-059, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE RESTATING IN ITS
  ENTIRETY THE CITY OF PALMDALE MASTER SCHEDULE OF
  FEES AND PENALTIES AND REPEALING ALL PRIOR
  ENACTMENTS INCONSISTENT WITH THIS RESOLUTION

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-059, a
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Palmdale restating in its entirety the City of
Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees and Penalties and repealing all prior enactments
inconsistent with this resolution.

BACKGROUND

The State Constitution authorizes cities to impose user and regulatory fees on services
and activities. However, the fees may not exceed the estimated reasonable cost of
providing the service or performing the activity.

Periodically, the City Council adopts Fee Resolutions, which 1) revise existing fees,
rates, or charges; 2) establish new fees, rates, or charges; or 3) revise headings or
descriptive language for existing fees for the City’s operating departments. Fee
adjustments are necessary to keep pace with inflation and recover costs.

DISCUSSION

To better achieve the City’s policy regarding cost recovery goals and to minimize General
Fund subsidies for services provided, staff proposes adjustments to the Fee Schedule as
outlined in the attached City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees and Penalties.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI) monthly,
which compares the current prices for consumer goods to those one year ago. The
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-059
June 26, 2024
Page 2

Consumer Price Index from April 2023 to April 2024 measured an increase in the price of
overall goods of 3.9%. The proposed fee schedule incorporates an increase to all City
imposed fees based on the CPI for the Greater Los Angeles area from April 2023 to April
2024 by 3.9%. Adjusting by the CPI allows the City to increase fees gradually to offset
expenditure increases better and avoid drastic measures in future years.

Any action by the City to levy a new fee or service charge or to approve an increase in an
existing fee or service must be approved by ordinance or resolution. Before any new fee
or service charge can be added to the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees, a public
hearing must be held, and reasonable notice must be provided to the community
members.

As such, Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-059 and
repeal all prior enactments inconsistent with it, authorizing the proposed adjustments to
the City of Palmdale Master Schedule of Fees and Penalties, effective July 1, 2024.

A Public Hearing Notice was published in the local newspaper of general circulation on
June 11, 2024, June 18, 2024, and June 25, 2024. At that time, the public was invited to
make oral and written presentations as part of the regularly scheduled meeting.
Additionally, written notice has been provided to interested parties who filed written
requests for mailed notice of the meeting on new or increased development-related fees
or service charges at least 14 days before the public meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT

Resolution No. CC 2024-059, if adopted, would allow for certain adjustments to fees and
the implementation of policies, resulting in increased revenues that offset the cost of
providing services.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.

  A. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

services by revising its schedule of City-Wide Master Schedule of Fees and Penalties;

above, the City made available for public inspection information required under
Government Code Section 66000, et seq.; and

to the City resulting therefrom, which justify the requested waiver or reduction of fees,
rates, or charges. The City Manager may consider the application and waive or reduce
such a fee, rate, or charge upon finding it of extraordinary benefit to the City. The
recipient of the relief granted by the City Manager must indemnify and defend the City
against all legal challenges which, from time to time, may be brought against the City or
any official of the City for, or as a result of, matters arising from such relief, directly or
indirectly. The determination of the City Manager shall be final and conclusive.

Definitions:
1. Agencies with proof of Internal Revenue Code IRC 501 (c) (3) (4) (5) and (6) are considered non-profits.
2. Commercial use is defined as an event held for the purpose of generating monetary gain for the event sponsor(s).
3. Direct program costs are exclusively incurred as a result of the program and are frequently variable, adjusting as program participation
  varies. Direct cost examples include part-time personnel, supplies, contract services and equipment. DryTown direct costs include the
  preceding expenses in addition to: full-time salaries, park utilities and equipment.
4. Indirect program costs that are shared among several programs and are necessary to execute general day-to-day operations. Indirect
  cost examples include personnel overhead, utilities and custodial expenses. Indirect costs are not considered as fees and charges
  are determined.
Policies
1. Non-profit with verifiable status of IRC 501 (c) (3) (4) (5) or (6) are eligible for a 25% facility reservation rate reduction. Unless otherwise
  specified, facility reservation fees that are eligible for a rate reduction are noted by an *. Rate reductions do not apply to personnel fees,
  facility deposits or equipment rental. Similarly, program fees for non-residents will increase 25% and DryTown admission fees for
  non-residents will increase 15%. Services subject to non-resident increase are noted by an **.
2. Unless otherwise specified, the rate for use of facilities for commercial purposes shall be charged at 200% of the hourly reservation fee,
  in addition to 5% gross admission ticket sales and gross alcohol sales. These fees may be reduced or waived if the applicant can
  demonstrate that residents of the City of Palmdale benefit from the use of facilities or the services being provided.
3. Unless otherwise specified, set-up and clean-up charges are comprised of applicable facility hourly reservation rates.
4. Park parking lots are generally not available for exclusive use reservations. If exclusivity can be accommodated and if parking fees are
  charged by the renter, 25% of parking fees collected are to be paid to the City.
5. Parks & Recreation program and service fees are established by following specified cost recovery policies. Fees and charges are
  determined by identifying direct costs if providing services and apply the cost recovery goals stated below. Direct program costs are
  referenced in the definitions section. It is widely accepted that park and recreation systems are publicly financed, and therefore offer free
  or affordable services. The level of program subsidy will be based on an assessment of the community or social benefit, local market and
  economic conditions. As services have a greater appeal to individuals or groups of individuals, it is appropriate to charge fees for the
  services at an increasing rate of cost recovery. Cost recovery target categories include: Community Benefit/Access, free; Community
  Benefit, 0-25%; Balanced Beneficiaries, 25-50%; Substantial Individual Benefit, 50-75%; Exclusive Individual Benefit, 75-100%.
  Cost recovery categories are further defined in Exhibit L-1.
General Fees
1. Unless otherwise specified, a special event application processing fee of $250 may be charged for staff services required to process the
  application, which may include coordination with other City departments, or State and County government agencies. The fee is
  non-refundable and does not guarantee approval of the application.
2. Unless otherwise specified, fees for personnel shall be calculated at hourly rate for staff wages, plus 45% for full-time benefits or 15%
  for part-time benefits and a 25% administrative fee. Unless the use warrants otherwise, staff will be scheduled to be on-site
  one-half hour before and after use. All personnel charges are a two-hour minimum.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council introduce and adopt Ordinance No. 1643, an
Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Palmdale, recommending City Council
approval of General Plan Amendment (GPA) 24-0002, Zone Change (ZC) 24-0002, and
Comprehensive Development Plan (CDEV) 24-0003 finding that the project is consistent
with Program Environmental Impact Report (PEIR) 22-002 prepared and certified in
conjunction with the City’s General Plan (Palmdale 2045) and direct staff to make
necessary modifications to the Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan (SP).

BACKGROUND

On June 13, 2024, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. PC-2024-014
recommending City Council approval of the proposed project to amend the boundary of
the SP and modify the General Plan Designation and zone of 12 parcels, totaling
approximately 59 acres within the SP area to Regional Commercial (RC).

The SP was adopted on December 15, 2020, to guide the development of a pedestrian-
oriented mixed-use district surrounding the City of Palmdale’s Transportation Center
with the future California high-speed rail (CAHSR) station. The SP replaced, in its
entirety, the original Palmdale Transit Village Specific Plan (PTVSP), adopted in 2007.

The 2007 PTVSP suggested a Transit Oriented Development surrounding the City’s
Transportation Center, which is served by local buses and regional Metrolink rail. With
the introduction of CAHSR in the region, Palmdale will experience a new era of growth,
thereby increasing interest and development around the new Palmdale Station hub.

Since 2020, there has been one amendment to the SP, not including the proposed
CDEV 24-0003. The SP area is bounded by Technology Drive to the north, 10th Street
East to the east, Palmdale Boulevard to the south, and State Route 14 (SR-14) to the
west.

DISCUSSION

CDEV 22-001 has been initiated to revise the SP boundary along the southwestern
portion of the SP to remove 12 parcels as shown in Figure 2. With the modification to the
SP boundary, GPA 24-0002 and ZC 24-0002 is a request to amend the General Plan
Land Use designation and zone of the 12 parcels from SP to RC. The amendment would
permit all the uses allowed within the RC zone pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code
Table 17.47.020-1 (Allowed Uses – Commercial/Office Zones). In addition, the proposed
amendment is beneficial to the City because it provides flexibility for future development
to a prominent entry point in the City, will address split zoning, and will assist in creating
synergy for the acquisition of Palmdale Boulevard. Furthermore, no development is
proposed in conjunction with this request.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

PEIR 22-002 (State Clearinghouse # 2021060494) was prepared and certified by the City
Council (Resolution No. CC 2022-096) on September 21, 2022, for approval of the City’s
General Plan (Palmdale 2045). As part of the environmental analysis, PEIR 22-002 also
considered the adoption and implementation of the Comprehensive Zoning Code and
Map update. Staff review has determined that a subsequent or supplemental PEIR as

described in California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15162,
15163, or 15164, is not required because the proposed GPA, ZC, and CDEV modify the

importance that will involve new significant environmental effects or increase the severity
of previously identified significant effects. As such, staff concluded that the request is
consistent with the previous PEIR in accordance with CEQA Guidelines and has

  The proposed application requests to change the General Plan land use and
  zoning designation for 12 parcels, totaling approximately 59 acres, from Specific
  Plan (SP) to Regional Commercial (RC). This change is beneficial to the City and
  will allow for more flexibility in future development of the site. If approved, the
  application would permit all uses allowed within the RC zone as outlined in the
  Palmdale Municipal Code Table 17.47.020-1 (Allowed Uses – Commercial/Office
  Zones). The RC General Plan Land Use designation and zone is intended for
  commercial/retail and service uses targeted at consumers from a regional market
  area. RC areas are designed to accommodate long-term goods and services
  such as big box retailers. In addition, the proposed amendment is beneficial to
  the City because it provides flexibility for future development to a prominent entry
  point in the City, will address split zoning, and will assist in creating synergy for
  the acquisition of Palmdale Boulevard.

  No development is proposed in conjunction with the request; with the approval of
  this project, any future development is required to comply with the development
  standards of the RC zone.
